text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Estonia will allocate 15 million kroons for discounts on student tickets on trains and buses. Officials hope private carriers will work out their own discount financing schemes.
- Estonia and Norway signed an agreement on the extradition of illegal immigrants. Visa-free travel between the two may be introduced in 1997.
- The trial over a major art theft case from the Art Museum has begun in Tallinn City Court.
- Tartu University, Estonia's largest and oldest university, plans to insure its buildings at an estimated cost of 80 million kroons.
- A recent survey by Saar Poll shows 47 percent of respondents would have preferred Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi to have resigned during the government crisis in November 1996.
- The world's media is very interested in a new theory on the development of the universe, which was worked out with the help of Estonian scientist Jaan Einasto.
- Creditors' representatives are to take over managing three large food stores owned by insolvent the Kadarik chain.
- The Singapore Tolaram Group plans this year to invest 90 million kroons in a textile plant it owns in Tallinn.
- The transit share in Tallinn Port's turnover grew by 10 percent in 1996, reaching 10 million tonnes.
